fix_escape_sequence.py.summary: Rewrite string literals that raise ``SyntaxWarning: invalid escape sequence``.
details: Tokenizes each module, detects backslash sequences that are not valid escapes and either prefixes the literal with ``r`` (when it contains no valid escapes) or doubles the offending backslashes. ``--dry-run`` reports the files without writing, ``--quiet`` hides the per-file lines.

fix_html_md_broken_links.py.summary: Repair relative links in Markdown and HTML files against a static directory.
details: Walks the current directory, and for every ``href`` whose target does not exist locally but does exist under ``/sdcard/_static`` rewrites the link to the absolute path. The original file is kept as ``.bak``.

fix_shebang_opt.py.summary: Point the shebangs of Python scripts at the current interpreter path.
details: Rewrites ``#!...python`` lines (``env``, ``/usr/bin``, Homebrew or Termux prefixes) to ``#!$PREFIX/bin/python3.14`` and restores the executable bit, skipping files whose shebang already matches.

fixcape.py.summary: Make Python string literals escape-safe so they stop warning.
details: Scans string tokens for invalid escapes and rewrites the literal either as a raw string or with the backslashes doubled, then writes the module back when something changed. Files are collected recursively from the current directory.

fixparanthes.py.summary: Fix unbalanced or JSON-bracket parentheses inside the strings of a JSON file.
details: Walks every string value, converts ``[``/``{`` into ``(`` (and the closing counterparts) and pads missing parentheses, then validates the result with :func:`json.loads` and rewrites the file with two-space indentation.

fixshebang.py.summary: Normalize the shebang of every Python file below the current directory.
details: Rewrites ``#!...python2/3`` lines to ``#!/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/env python`` and processes the files in a worker pool, reporting how many shebangs were changed.

fixwhl.py.summary: Rename wheels that were mangled by a bulk rename back to their canonical name.
details: Opens each ``.whl`` in the current directory, reads ``Name``/``Version`` from the bundled ``METADATA`` and renames the file to ``name-version-pyX-none-any.whl``, refusing to overwrite an existing file.

flaten.py.summary: Flatten a directory tree, moving every file into one folder.
details: Moves all files from the sub-directories into the target directory, renaming on collision so nothing is overwritten, and removes the directories that became empty.

fmt_bash.py.summary: Format shell scripts with ``shfmt`` in parallel.
details: Formats the files given on the command line or, without arguments, every file below the current directory that either ends in ``.sh`` or starts with a shell shebang. Files that fail to format are listed and, with ``--move``, copied into an ``error`` directory.

foext.py.summary: Sort the files of the current directory into folders named after their extension.
details: Every top-level file is moved into ``<extension>/`` (``no_extension`` for files without a suffix), leaving the sub-directories untouched.

foldesiz.py.summary: Distribute the files below a directory into folders grouped by file size.
details: Collects the files (skipping the usual noise directories), sorts them by size and moves them into numbered folders that each hold a similar number of files and a similar size range, so batches of comparable size can be processed together.

foldext.py.summary: Folderize a whole tree by file extension and report the per-extension totals.
details: Walks the current directory recursively, moves every file into a top-level folder named after its lower-case extension (``no_extension`` when absent), removes the emptied directories and prints a table of file counts and sizes per extension.

foldimension.py.summary: Sort images into folders named after their pixel dimensions.
details: Reads each image (JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WebP, ICO) with Pillow, derives a ``WIDTHxHEIGHT`` name and moves the file into that folder, keeping both names when the target already exists.

foldpy.py.summary: Group the Python files of the current directory by whether they parse cleanly.
details: Compiles each ``.py`` file in a process pool and sorts the results into ``ok``, ``warn`` (raised a ``SyntaxWarning``) and ``error`` (unreadable or invalid syntax). It only lists the groups unless ``--apply`` is given, in which case the files are moved into matching folders.
